issues.legal_issue: Unequal distribution of a testator’s assets among family members does not, by itself, make a will unnatural or create suspicion about its execution.
material_facts: The will distributed immovable property unevenly among the children, gave nothing to the husband and one daughter, and distributed movable property equally among the sons.
The daughter who received nothing supported the will rather than challenging it.
The challenging daughter had received some property by gift during the testator’s lifetime, and the record disclosed acrimony between her and her father.
issues.conclusion: The uneven distribution, by itself, did not make the will unnatural or create suspicion about its execution; the contrary finding could not be sustained.
issues.legal_principle: The choice of how to distribute property under a will lies within the testator’s discretion. Unequal distribution among children, by itself, is not a suspicious circumstance surrounding execution. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.will_challenged_in_civil_suit: A person challenged a will in a civil suit.

predicates.unequal_distribution_is_only_basis_for_s: The claim that execution was suspicious rested only on the uneven distribution of property.

issues.definition: If a will is challenged in a civil suit and uneven distribution among family members is the only asserted basis for suspicion, that distribution alone is not suspicious.

issues.legal_issue: The failure to register a will does not, by itself, create doubt about its execution merely because another family member’s will was registered.
material_facts: The testator’s will was unregistered, while her husband’s will was registered.
An attesting witness to both wills explained that the husband had insisted on registration of his will because litigation had arisen over his wife’s will.
issues.conclusion: The difference in registration did not create doubt about the due execution of the testator’s will.
issues.legal_principle: The fact that one will was registered and another was not does not, without more, cast doubt on execution; the judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.related_will_is_registered: A related family member’s will was registered.

issues.legal_issue: A failure to mention a will in later correspondence does not create suspicion about its execution where the will had been raised in earlier proceedings and disclosed in other relevant proceedings.
material_facts: The challenger relied on the will not being mentioned in correspondence exchanged with her father after the testator’s death.
The challenger’s own case was that the will had been set up in earlier litigation between siblings, and that litigation preceded the correspondence.
The will had also been disclosed in estate-duty and wealth-tax proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The omission from the later correspondence did not establish suspicion about due execution in the circumstances of the case.
issues.legal_principle: An omission in correspondence must be assessed in its context; it did not create suspicion here given the earlier reference to the will and its disclosure in other proceedings. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.will_raised_in_earlier_proceedings: The will had been raised in proceedings that preceded the correspondence.

issues.definition: If a will omitted from later correspondence had already been raised in earlier proceedings and disclosed in other relevant proceedings, the omission does not create execution suspicion.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot draw a presumption against those supporting a will for failing to produce documents for signature comparison when the will’s execution was proved by an attesting witness and the challenger did not seek production of the comparison documents.
material_facts: An attesting witness testified to the testator signing the will in the witnesses’ presence and the witnesses signing in the testator’s presence.
The challenger disputed the will but did not take steps to obtain documents containing the testator’s admitted signatures for comparison.
The documents the challenger did produce were not shown to contain the testator’s signatures.
issues.conclusion: No presumption could be drawn against those supporting the will for not producing other documents to compare signatures.
issues.legal_principle: Where an attesting witness proves execution and the challenger has not sought production of documents for signature comparison, the judgment’s stated circumstances do not justify a presumption against the will’s supporters for not producing those documents. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that a will was unproved cannot stand where an attesting witness formally proved execution and the circumstances relied on to discredit the will did not establish suspicion sufficient to overturn the trial court’s finding.
material_facts: The trial court found the will duly proved after relying on an attesting witness’s testimony.
The appellate court accepted that there was formal evidence of execution but reversed the trial court based on the will’s distribution and other asserted circumstances.
The Supreme Court found that the uneven distribution and the other circumstances relied on did not sustain the finding that the will was unnatural or unproved.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the will had not been proved was set aside, the trial court’s judgment was restored, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: The judgment relied on the attesting witness’s formal evidence of execution and held that the identified circumstances did not justify rejecting the will. It cites no statutory provision or earlier case in reaching this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_reversal_of_trial_court_w: An appeal challenges an appellate decision that reversed a trial court’s finding that a will was proved.
predicates.attesting_witness_formally_proved_execut: An attesting witness gave formal evidence that the testator and witnesses signed the will in each other’s presence.
predicates.relied_on_circumstances_do_not_establish: The circumstances relied on to reject the will do not establish suspicion sufficient to discredit its execution.

issues.definition: In an appeal against reversal of a trial court’s finding, formal proof by an attesting witness coupled with circumstances insufficient to establish execution suspicion means the will is proved and the trial court’s finding is restored.
